text:
alex.k: FYI customer on Dedicated (VPC) reporting intermittent 503s and TLS handshake failures when clients in us-west call model endpoints hosted in eu-west. Seen ~every 15-30m.

maria_s: ugh. any logs or repro steps from the customer?

alex.k: they captured the client side curl error and the server logs. curl shows TLS handshake "alert handshake_failure". server logs show connection from a different IP than expected and cert presented is for service.eu.internal but client received cert with CN=service.us-west.internal in some failures.

alex.k: repro commands they ran:
```
# from us-west host
dig @10.0.0.2 service.internal A +short
curl -v https://service.internal/api/health --resolve service.internal:443:10.20.30.40
# tcpdump on client during failure
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.20.30.40 and port 443 -w /tmp/fail.pcap
```

samir_net: hmm that points to split-horizon / private hosted zone mismatch + stale cache. If client resolves service.internal to an eu IP sometimes and us IP other times, SNI doesn't match cert. Are the private hosted zones associated to both VPCs?

alex.k: checked: Route53 private zone service.internal is associated to eu-west VPC, but there's also an older private zone with same name attached to us-west for legacy infra. We thought we removed it, but VPC association remained.

netops: also saw evidence of EDNS+UDP truncation on our side that caused some resolvers to fallback to TCP and hit a secondary resolver in another region. TCP fallback can surface stale A records from a peered resolver. Captured snippet from tcpdump: `DNS/UDP frag: truncation set, retrying TCP` and then subsequent TCP answer contained A record pointing to 10.20.30.40 (us-west).

maria_s: so resolution path is inconsistent depending on packet size and which resolver handles the TCP query. That explains the intermittent TLS CN mismatch. What's the customer NAT/egress setup? any caching proxy?

alex.k: customer uses an egress proxy with DNS cache+ACLs. It has an allowlist of resolver IPs and only forwards to the nearest resolver. When TCP fallback happens, traffic goes to their fallback resolver which still has the old us-west zone association.

samir_net: repro plan I suggest: 1) from customer host, run `dig +noedns` and `dig +edns=0` and `dig +ignore` to force different paths; 2) capture both UDP and TCP DNS answers; 3) check `ndots` and search domain behavior. Also run `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername service.internal` to see cert and SNI negotiation.

alex.k: customer ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.40:443 -servername service.internal -prexit` and got CN=service.us-west.internal. When they hit 10.21.50.12 (eu ip) they got CN=service.eu.internal.

netops: fix options:
- remove duplicate private hosted zone or re-associate only the correct zone with both VPCs (preferred split-horizon cleanup).
- reduce DNS TTL and clear caches on egress proxies while we roll the zone change.
- ensure EDNS is enabled on customer resolvers or increase UDP packet size (avoid truncation) so queries don't unexpectedly go to TCP and other resolvers.
- as a short-term mitigation, add a firewall rule to force DNS to go to a single trusted resolver IP (their primary) rather than allowing fallback to stale resolver.

samir_net: also check our cert rotation pipeline — certs are region-specific names. If they want the same cert across regions, we can issue SAN certs for both FQDNs, but that's a product change. Better to fix DNS.

ingrid-bot: ticket INF-7892 created for cross-region DNS cleanup and customer-facing incident note. Assigned to netops and platform eng. :white_check_mark:

alex.k: next steps I've asked customer to: 1) flush egress proxy DNS cache; 2) run the diagnostic dig+tcpdump commands and share pcaps; 3) temporarily pin service.internal to eu ip via /etc/hosts to confirm behavior. I'll update ticket with results.

maria_s: thanks. keeping this thread for updates. if we need emergency rollback or cert SANs, ping me and infra-ops. :thumbsup:
